messages:
hana_devexp: Customer ping: trying `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/repo.git@main` and getting `Could not build wheels for redwood-sdk` on macOS arm with Python 3.11. They also said top-level import `from redwood import AsyncClient` fails after pip install but works in editable mode.

omar_engineering: editable masking is classic. When you `pip install -e .` imports hit local files so missing exports or packaging omissions don't show. Wheel/sdist paths expose missing MANIFEST entries or missing `__all__` exports.

lina_packaging: quick local audit showed three problems: 1) pyproject uses poetry-core which requires fairly recent pip/build to install from VCS; 2) `redwood/py.typed` missing from sdist so typing marker absent; 3) `redwood/__init__.py` doesn't re-export AsyncClient so `from redwood import AsyncClient` fails when installed as a wheel.

ivy_support: user also reported a dependency conflict when pip tried to resolve versions (poetry.lock pins older importlib-metadata). They see resolver picking a combination that triggers a C-extension compile on arm and then wheel build fails.

oma r_engineering: two-pronged approach: short-term patch to fix packaging metadata and exports, long-term to add built wheels for macos/arm and a reproducible install doc. For quick fix: add `include redwood/py.typed` in MANIFEST.in (and tool.poetry.include in pyproject), add `from .async_client import AsyncClient` in `redwood/__init__.py`, and either switch build-system to setuptools+wheel or state `pip>=23` in docs.

lina_packaging: I'll open a small PR with those three changes plus a CI smoke test that creates a clean venv, `pip install dist/*.whl`, and runs `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient; import pkgutil; print(bool(pkgutil.get_data('redwood','py.typed')))"`. That should catch the editable-vs-wheel gap.

qa-bot: Automated test suggestion: add a packaging test that actually installs an sdist too: `pip install dist/*.tar.gz` and import check. Added to the packaging matrix ticket.

ivy_support: workaround I sent to the customer: upgrade pip and build tooling then build wheel locally: `python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel build` then `python -m build` and `pip install dist/redwood-*.whl`. For poetry users: `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o reqs.txt && pip install -r reqs.txt`. Also warned them that poetry.lock isn't used by `pip install git+...` so that can change resolver behavior.

omar_engineering: long-term: add cibuildwheel to release pipeline to publish manylinux and macOS universal2 wheels so consumer pip doesn't attempt local compiles on arm. Also add a small check in release process to verify that `py.typed` exists in the built artifacts.

lina_packaging: noted. PR will include MANIFEST.in entry, __init__ export, and the packaging smoke test. I'll also update INSTALL.md and CONTRIBUTING.md with the pip vs poetry guidance and the recommended `pip` versions.

hana_devexp: thanks  can we also add a tiny note in the SDK changelog that old pip versions may fail on VCS installs and that we published wheels for arm? That will save future tickets.

ivy_support: will follow-up with the affected customer after PR/CI and publish patch wheel if CI green. Ticket updated. :thumbsup:
